task: This is a synthetic writing exercise. Using these fictional reporting notes, write a newspaper reported feature for general readers. Draw only on the supplied notes; do not invent additional reported events, scenes, or quotations. Write from this reporting snapshot as of April 10, 2025. Include a headline. Target 450 to 650 words. Follow AP style.

facts.text: The town of Ridgemont, New Mexico (pop. 3,800), is approximately 22 miles from the proposed Granite Basin deep geological nuclear waste repository, which received its construction license in April 2025.

Ridgemont retired teacher Claudette Moreau, 72, has opposed the repository since its first proposal in 1994; she founded a citizens' group that has filed seven administrative challenges over 30 years.
Moreau said: "My students graduated and moved away. I stayed because someone has to. In thirty years of fighting this, I have not changed one vote. But I have made sure they were slow."

Rancher Hector Vega, 55, whose property borders the site boundary, has cautiously supported the project since 2019 when the government offered an economic development package for Ridgemont County tied to the repository's approval.
Vega said: "I don't love having a nuclear waste facility next door. But I live next door to poverty too. And poverty doesn't come with $140 million in infrastructure money."

The development package includes a new highway bypass, a water treatment plant upgrade, and a job training center; Ridgemont County officials estimate the repository will directly employ 180 people at wages averaging $68,000 per year.

The Kwena Nation, whose members have treaty rights to land within 30 kilometers of the site, formally objected throughout the licensing process; tribal liaison James Silvercloud said the tribe was never given meaningful consultation, only notification.
Silvercloud said: "There is a difference between being consulted and being told what has already been decided. We have always been told."

The Nuclear Regulatory Authority determined that the Granite Basin geology met long-term isolation standards; three independent geologists who reviewed the record supported the finding, but two others published dissenting papers on water infiltration modeling.
Ridgemont's grocery store, hardware store, and two restaurants closed between 2015 and 2023; the repository supporters say it represents the town's best realistic employment prospect.

Moreau said she accepts that her legal challenges will not stop construction: "At my age, winning means the record is correct. It means someone reads these filings in a hundred years and knows this was not done with consent."

Vega's ranch produces cattle and limited water; he said the repository's presence has not yet affected his property value, but he has accepted that he cannot sell easily: "Who's going to buy a ranch next to that? I've chosen to stay."

County Commission chair Leticia Durán said the vote to accept the economic development package was 4–1, with the sole dissenting vote citing concerns about transport risk along the county's two-lane state highway.
The repository's waste transport plan routes shipments along existing rail lines; no shipments will use the county highway, according to the licensing record.

Silvercloud said the tribe will pursue legal remedies but does not expect to prevail; he said the case is important for establishing a record of inadequate consultation that future tribal advocates can use.

Moreau and Vega have never met in person despite living eight miles apart; the town's repository debate has been conducted through public hearings and county newsletters rather than direct community dialogue.
The repository construction is expected to create 400 temporary construction jobs; permanent employment will phase in as waste acceptance begins, projected for 2032.
Ridgemont's population has declined 22% since 2000; school enrollment is down 35%; county officials say without the repository, the fiscal trajectory is continued decline.
Moreau said she voted in every election for 54 years and will vote in every election she has left: "That's the only power I have. I'll use it."
Vega said he intends to retire before waste deliveries begin: "By then, my son will decide what comes next for the ranch. It's his problem now. I made it survivable for him to have a problem."
